name: software-knowledge
description: Durable software semantics, decisions, constraints, architecture, operations, and reusable engineering knowledge
purpose: Reduce the cost of future software design, review, operation, and incident response
Preserve intent and constraints that cannot be reliably reconstructed from the current implementation

include: capabilities, observable behavior, rules, and data semantics
stable system responsibilities and interface meaning
architecture decisions, alternatives, trade-offs, and invalidation conditions
operational procedures, failure modes, and quality strategy
reusable concepts, patterns, and engineering skills
exclude: call graphs and dependency paths derivable from CodeGraph
mechanically reproducible API, schema, or configuration dumps
routine fixes and transient task telemetry

retain: failure modes, recovery knowledge, and empirical lessons
risks, unresolved questions, and invalidation conditions
omit: facts that CodeGraph can reliably regenerate from the current repository
implementation detail without explanatory or decision value
raw logs, test output, meeting chronology, and source-document restatement

authorities: source documents and decision records at their recorded revision
repository and tests at the recorded Git revision
checks: CodeGraph anchor replay when code structure matters
test or contract reference for executable invariants
explicit marking of inferred and disputed rationale

triggers: business rule or interface contract changes
incident evidence changes an operational conclusion

priorities: business term, rule, and behavior match
verified source and current Git binding
stable code anchors before stored implementation detail
typed paths across domain, capability, system, and interface pages
